## 7b0c20fe6f33

**Possible shortcut/domain restriction plus reproduced override defect.** For
generator SHA-256 `53cefe1ef32348049cc70c5a8e4a3abd72cefb0efba9402e463541652f29f394`,
300 default draws (100 each in easy/medium/hard) all contained exactly four color-3
cells and used only four small vectors: `(-1,+2)`, `(+1,+2)`, `(+2,-1)`, and
`(+2,+1)`. The distribution was identical by band. Canonical examples instead use
a three-cell connected motif and larger vectors such as `(+4,+5)`, `(-4,+3)`, and
`(+5,+1)`. A learner trained only on this generator can therefore adopt the narrow
rule “copy four green cells using one of four small offsets,” which does not cover
the canonical domain.

The advertised `vector_choice` control is also inert: with the same seed/sample,
values 0 and 3 produced byte-identical grids and the same observed vector; unknown
keys were accepted. Exact counts and the replayable probe are in
`checks/audit/audit_probe.json`. The attempted official override run was interrupted
before controller finalization and is retained at `checks/audit-7b0-override/`; I do
not treat that incomplete run as a verdict. I did not modify this audit target.
